gen-irish-grover-gf-pt-sans-caption: Big-bodied lowercase with unclosed, inviting bowls makes the text easy to step into. PT Sans Caption stays plain and steady while Irish Grover's heading letters shimmer faintly in weight, and that textural gap is the pair's real appeal.
gen-irish-grover-gf-puritan: Puritan reads soft and rounded, its oversized e and a counters staying open to the side. But shrink Irish Grover and its crossbars, a touch thinner than the stems, start to look timid.
gen-irish-grover-gf-questrial: Fun and organic, Irish Grover draws curved strokes that lighten mildly toward their ends. Questrial, a sans-serif drawn as if with a fixed pen, keeps every stroke flat and uniform beneath it.
gen-irish-grover-gf-radio-canada: Sturdy words over a straight-laced line, with Irish Grover's moderate contrast leading the way. Radio Canada, a sans-serif with no stress in its curves, does the quiet work of carrying text while the heading handles the personality.
gen-irish-grover-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big is a monoline sans-serif that fills its line. Its bowls match the stem thickness, so Irish Grover's brush strokes, with only slight pressure changes, stand out as the livelier voice.
gen-irish-grover-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro is a sans with broad terminal gaps and a constant weight running from word to word. And Irish Grover earns its keep big and brief, where mild weight shifts smooth out the reading pace.
gen-irish-grover-gf-roboto: A lightly tilted nib seems to have shaped Irish Grover's sturdy letters. Roboto handles the steady reading, its generous round letters low in contrast, while the heading supplies the character.
gen-irish-grover-gf-saira: Saira is a sans-serif whose s shows daylight and whose round letters stretch high. Saira does the quiet readable work, while Irish Grover shows off a modest weight shift across every curve.
gen-irish-grover-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch is a compact sans-serif with a clearly open mouth on its lowercase e. And Irish Grover, its weight shifting like thread against yarn, handles the play while Sarpanch handles the plain talking.
gen-irish-grover-gf-savate: Savate is a sans-serif with sturdy hairlines and open jaws on every curve. Yet Irish Grover's large, sturdy, open-throated letters make the clearest difference, organic against Savate's contemporary tidiness.
